conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Hi, I’m Dr. Lee. You’re admitted for left rib pain. Can you tell me what happened?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. This morning, I lifted my bag and suddenly felt sharp pain on my left side. It’s different from my usual belly pain—more on the surface and worse with movement.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I see. You went to the ED earlier. They did a chest X-ray and it didn’t show any fractures or lung issues. You also declined a CT scan to avoid more radiation, correct?

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Yes. I’ve had so many scans over the years. I didn’t want another unless absolutely necessary.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That makes sense. The X-ray showed no broken ribs. Given your osteoporosis, we’re considering a muscle strain or minor rib injury. We’ll treat it as musculoskeletal pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. But I’ve been in a lot of pain. I asked for Toradol in the ED—can I get that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Yes, we’re starting Toradol twice a day. We’re also giving you a Lidoderm patch for the rib area. It should help reduce the pain over the next day.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Thank you. I’ve also been struggling with anxiety and sleep. Can I get something for that?

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We can continue your home dose of trazodone at night. We’re avoiding IV benzodiazepines unless absolutely needed, especially with your complex pain history.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Good morning. How’s the rib pain now? We checked on you overnight and you seemed to be resting more comfortably.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: It’s a little better, but my belly pain is worse today. I need IV Dilaudid. I’ve been on a pain contract with my pain doctor, and this is what I take.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand, but we consulted the pain team. IV Dilaudid can slow your gut even more and make your abdominal symptoms worse. It’s not recommended for your type of chronic GI pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: But it’s what works for me. If I don’t get it, I’ll have to leave. I can’t stay here in this pain.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I hear how frustrated you are. We’re continuing your home morphine suppository, Toradol, and the Lidoderm patch. We’re also giving ketorolac. These are safer options for you.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: They don’t help like Dilaudid. I want to go home. If you won’t give me what I need, I’d rather leave.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I’m sorry you feel that way. Medically, you’re stable. Your rib pain is improving, and there’s no sign of infection or fracture. We don’t think IV Dilaudid is safe, but you’re okay to go home if you choose.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve prepared your discharge. You’re going home with the Lidoderm patch and your regular medications. We’re increasing your Lovenox dose for blood clot prevention.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Okay. I just want to get out of here. The pain’s still there, but I’ll manage at home.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: I understand. Please follow up with your pain doctor and GI specialist. Call us if the rib pain gets worse or you have trouble breathing.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thank you for trying, even if we didn’t agree on everything.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We care about your comfort and safety. Take care, and I hope you feel better soon.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Your discharge paperwork is ready. You’re cleared to go home with services. A walker will be provided, and home health will check in.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: Good. I just want to be in my own space.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: We’ve updated your GI doctor and pain clinic. They’ll be expecting your call. Please keep your appointments.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I will. Thanks again.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: Take these prescriptions for the Lidoderm patch and acetaminophen, though I know you said they don’t help much. Use them if needed.

conversation_lines.speaker: Patient
conversation_lines.text: I’ll try. I mostly just need rest and my routine.

conversation_lines.speaker: Doctor
conversation_lines.text: That’s fair. We’re here if you need us. Please reach out if anything changes. Take care.
